sentences.en: It really is almost everything.
sentences.zh: 这确实几乎涵盖了一切。

sentences.en: Infrastructure is just about everything that makes civilization physically possible.
sentences.zh: 基础设施几乎是使文明在物理层面成为可能的一切事物。

sentences.en: Roads, bridges, water supply, sewage removal, dams, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 道路、桥梁、供水、污水处理、大坝等等。

sentences.en: The physical part of civilization is the infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 文明的物理部分就是基础设施。

sentences.en: That's Henry Petrosky.
sentences.zh: 那是亨利·佩特罗斯基。

sentences.en: Well, my name is Henry Petrosky.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我叫亨利·佩特罗斯基。

sentences.en: I'm a professor of civil engineering and history at Duke University.
sentences.zh: 我是杜克大学的土木工程与历史学教授。

sentences.en: He's written a number of books about catastrophic failures in engineering
sentences.zh: 他写过许多关于工程灾难性故障的书，

sentences.en: and also one about the history of the toothpick.
sentences.zh: 还有一本关于牙签历史的书。

sentences.en: So he's one of us.
sentences.zh: 所以他是我们的一员。

sentences.en: His most recent book is all about infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他最近的一本书讲的正是基础设施。

sentences.en: The name of the book is The Road Taken, The History and Future of America's Infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 书名是《走过的路：美国基础设施的历史与未来》。

sentences.en: A couple weeks ago, I interviewed Dr. Petrosky about his book and the state of infrastructure in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我采访了佩特罗斯基博士，谈论了他的书以及美国基础设施的现状。

sentences.en: The first of many things that I learned that shocked me
sentences.zh: 我学到的第一件让我震惊的事情是，

sentences.en: was that the word infrastructure itself is actually kind of new to English.
sentences.zh: “基础设施”这个词本身在英语中其实相当新。

sentences.en: What we call infrastructure today used to be called public works.
sentences.zh: 我们今天所说的基础设施，过去被称为公共工程。

sentences.en: And in America, public works was probably a familiar term up until the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 在美国，“公共工程”这个词在20世纪80年代之前可能还是个熟悉的术语。

sentences.en: But public works became a term closely associated with what was called pork barrel,
sentences.zh: 但“公共工程”后来与所谓的“猪肉桶政治”紧密联系在一起，

sentences.en: which was also considered a rather pejorative term
sentences.zh: 这也被认为是一个相当贬义的词，

sentences.en: because it had to do with building things that were considered unnecessary or wasteful.
sentences.zh: 因为它与建造被认为不必要或浪费的项目有关。

sentences.en: Pork barrel is government spending pushed forward by a congressperson
sentences.zh: “猪肉桶政治”是指国会议员推动的政府支出，

sentences.en: to solely benefit the people in their home district.
sentences.zh: 旨在专门造福其选区的民众。

sentences.en: It was associated with politics that was tit for tat.
sentences.zh: 它与那种礼尚往来的政治挂钩。

sentences.en: You vote for my pork, I'll vote for yours.
sentences.zh: 你投我的猪肉桶项目一票，我就投你的。

sentences.en: But the connection between public works and government corruption got even worse than trading votes.
sentences.zh: 但公共工程与政府腐败之间的联系变得比选票交易更糟糕。

sentences.en: It reached its peak in 1973.
sentences.zh: 它在1973年达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: There was a major scandal that one of our vice presidents of the United States had to resign,
sentences.zh: 当时发生了一起重大丑闻，导致我们的一位美国副总统不得不辞职，

sentences.en: Spiro Agnew, because he basically was taking money for road contracts in his home state of Maryland.
sentences.zh: 他就是斯皮罗·阿格纽，因为他基本上是在为家乡马里兰州的道路合同收受贿赂。

sentences.en: So in the 1980s, when shrinking government was becoming all the rage and pork barrel and earmarks
sentences.zh: 所以到了20世纪80年代，当缩减政府规模成为大趋势，而猪肉桶和专项拨款

sentences.en: were our biggest enemy after the Soviets, of course, the term public works fell out of fashion.
sentences.zh: 成为我们仅次于苏联的最大敌人时，“公共工程”这个词就过时了。

sentences.en: So infrastructure became a term that replaced public works generally.
sentences.zh: 于是“基础设施”成为了取代“公共工程”的通用术语。

sentences.en: But the term was still so new that in the 1980s,
sentences.zh: 但这个词当时还很新，以至于在20世纪80年代，

sentences.en: the Wall Street Journal put infrastructure within quotation marks.
sentences.zh: 《华尔街日报》还会把“基础设施”加上引号。

sentences.en: Since infrastructure is the physical part of civilization,
sentences.zh: 由于基础设施是文明的物理部分，

sentences.en: it's hard to generalize which government body or private party is responsible for each individual part of it.
sentences.zh: 很难一概而论哪个政府机构或私人方负责其中的每一个具体部分。

sentences.en: So in our conversation, we tended to focus on the big one.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的谈话中，我们倾向于关注大方向。

sentences.en: Well, let's take roads.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们以道路为例。

sentences.en: We tend to think of roads, especially highways,
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于认为道路，特别是高速公路，

sentences.en: as one of the wonderful things that the federal government does.
sentences.zh: 是联邦政府所做的了不起的事情之一。

sentences.en: Well, that's pretty much wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这基本上是错误的。

sentences.en: Roads today in the United States are largely the responsibility of municipalities and states.
sentences.zh: 如今美国的道路很大程度上是地方政府和州的责任。

sentences.en: One of the reasons that it's complicated like this is that the federal government
sentences.zh: 之所以如此复杂，原因之一是联邦政府

sentences.en: is not authorized by the Constitution to build roads or bridges or even fixing them up by itself.
sentences.zh: 并没有得到宪法授权去独自修建道路、桥梁，甚至连维修都不行。

sentences.en: It has to go through the states.
sentences.zh: 它必须通过各州来完成。

sentences.en: Article 1, Section 8 of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国宪法第一条第八款

sentences.en: Constitution states that the federal government can build post roads,
sentences.zh: 规定联邦政府可以修建邮政道路，

sentences.en: meaning routes for the post office to operate effectively,
sentences.zh: 即为了让邮局有效运作而设立的路线，

sentences.en: but no other kinds of roads are specified.
sentences.zh: 但没有指定其他类型的道路。

sentences.en: In fact, in 1817, when a bill was passed by Congress that approved the funding of internal improvements in the country,
sentences.zh: 事实上，1817年，当国会通过一项批准为国内改善工程提供资金的法案时，

sentences.en: like roads and canals, it was vetoed by then-President James Madison because he felt it was unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 比如道路和运河，时任总统詹姆斯·麦迪逊否决了它，因为他认为这违宪。

sentences.en: And he should know because he wrote the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 而且他应该很清楚，因为宪法就是他写的。

sentences.en: The federal government can give awards to the states.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府可以给各州拨款。

sentences.en: It could give grants to the states or municipalities, but it can't do it itself.
sentences.zh: 它可以给各州或地方政府提供补助，但它不能亲自去修。

sentences.en: But what the feds can do is put a tax on gasoline to raise money for roads,
sentences.zh: 但联邦政府能做的是对汽油征税来为道路筹集资金，

sentences.en: which they then give to the states and cities.
sentences.zh: 然后将这些资金分发给各州和城市。

sentences.en: This has been the case since the Revenue Act of 1932,
sentences.zh: 这种情况自1932年的《税收法案》以来一直如此，

sentences.en: which was passed by Herbert Hoover, which raised taxes on pretty much everything.
sentences.zh: 该法案由赫伯特·胡佛签署，几乎提高了所有东西的税收。

sentences.en: Presently, it's 18.4 cents per gallon.
sentences.zh: 目前，税率是每加仑18.4美分。

sentences.en: And that gives the federal government about $30 billion a year to distribute to the states.
sentences.zh: 这让联邦政府每年有大约300亿美元可以分发给各州。

sentences.en: And that distribution, the federal government exercises some control
sentences.zh: 通过这种分配，联邦政府行使了一定的控制权，

sentences.en: and enables it to provide some standardization to the roads,
sentences.zh: 并使其能够为道路提供一定的标准化，

sentences.en: which I consider a good thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: Because you don't really want to drive from one state to another
sentences.zh: 因为你肯定不想从一个州开车到另一个州时，

sentences.en: and find that the roads are completely different.
sentences.zh: 发现道路完全不同。

sentences.en: It was the federal government that brought all the states into unification
sentences.zh: 正是联邦政府通过道路标线的颜色，

sentences.en: with the colors of the lines on the roads.
sentences.zh: 实现了各州的统一。

sentences.en: Yellow lines divide traffic going different ways.
sentences.zh: 黄色标线分隔不同方向的车流。

sentences.en: White dashes divide lanes going the same way.
sentences.zh: 白色虚线分隔同向行驶的车道。

sentences.en: The federal government making the money contingent on following the standards
sentences.zh: 联邦政府将资金与遵守标准挂钩，

sentences.en: is what made that happen.
sentences.zh: 才促成了这一点。

sentences.en: But the $30 billion Federal Highway Trust Fund,
sentences.zh: 但是300亿美元的联邦公路信托基金，

sentences.en: which is fed by the National Gasoline Tax,
sentences.zh: 由全国汽油税提供支持，

sentences.en: isn't keeping up with our current needs.
sentences.zh: 已经无法满足我们当前的需求了。

sentences.en: One easy solution, of course, would be to increase the gasoline tax.
sentences.zh: 当然，一个简单的解决方案就是提高汽油税。

sentences.en: It hasn't been increased since 1993, which is quite a while.
sentences.zh: 自1993年以来它就没涨过，这已经是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Because the federal gas tax has been so stagnant,
sentences.zh: 由于联邦汽油税一直停滞不前，

sentences.en: the states take it upon themselves to levy their own state gas taxes
sentences.zh: 各州只能自行征收州汽油税，

sentences.en: and fund their road projects that way.
sentences.zh: 并以此资助他们的道路项目。

sentences.en: Increasing the federal gas tax is not popular,
sentences.zh: 提高联邦汽油税并不受欢迎，

sentences.en: so politicians have trouble doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以政客们很难做到这一点。

sentences.en: But even if they could, it isn't a great solution.
sentences.zh: 但即使他们能做到，这也不是一个好的解决方案。

sentences.en: Obviously, if you're going to depend upon the tax on gasoline per gallon
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你要依赖每加仑汽油的税收

sentences.en: for replenishing the fund,
sentences.zh: 来补充基金，

sentences.en: then you have to project how many gallons of gasoline are going to be used
sentences.zh: 那么你就必须预测将要消耗多少加仑的汽油，

sentences.en: and whether that volume of consumption is going to be steady or increase.
sentences.zh: 以及这种消费量是会保持稳定还是会增加。

sentences.en: And generally, we expect things like that to increase with time.
sentences.zh: 通常我们预期这类消费会随时间增加。

sentences.en: Right now, people are driving more electric and hybrid vehicles than ever before.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们驾驶电动和混合动力汽车的数量比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: They still use the roads, but they spend less money at the gas pump.
sentences.zh: 他们依然在使用道路，但在加油站花的钱却更少了。

sentences.en: So Prius owners may be saving the environment,
sentences.zh: 所以普锐斯车主可能是在拯救环境，

sentences.en: but they are mooching off our roads.
sentences.zh: 但他们却在免费使用我们的道路。

sentences.en: It is so hard to do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 做正确的事真是太难了。

sentences.en: So now there's a notion to separate the collecting of taxes
sentences.zh: 所以现在有一种想法，将征税与汽油消费分离开来，

sentences.en: needed to maintain the road from the consumption of gasoline.
sentences.zh: 以维持道路的维护。

sentences.en: Instead of taxing the fuel that's used,
sentences.zh: 不再对所使用的燃料征税，

sentences.en: you tax the mileage that the vehicle travels on state roads,
sentences.zh: 而是对车辆在州公路上行驶的里程征税，

sentences.en: regardless of whether it uses fuel or not.
sentences.zh: 无论它是否使用燃料。

sentences.en: And this can be done in a variety of ways.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过多种方式实现。

sentences.en: At present, there are a number of pilot programs that are trying this out.
sentences.zh: 目前，有许多试点项目正在尝试这种方法。

sentences.en: There are pilot programs that involve self-reporting the number of miles you drive.
sentences.zh: 有些试点项目涉及让车主自行报告行驶里程。

sentences.en: But the obvious solution is to have a GPS-based tracking device inside each car.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的解决方案是在每辆车里安装一个基于GPS的追踪设备。

sentences.en: And we'll see if that goes anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我们看看这是否行得通。

sentences.en: Because if you're someone who gets freaked out about the constitutionality of the federal government
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是一个对联邦政府修建道路的合宪性感到恐慌的人，

sentences.en: building roads, I'm going to guess that you're not going to be too keen on the federal government
sentences.zh: 我猜你肯定不会太乐意让联邦政府

sentences.en: installing a tracking device in your car to see how many miles you drive.
sentences.zh: 在你的车里安装追踪设备来查看你开了多少英里。

sentences.en: I suspect it will take at least a decade to replace the gas tax entirely.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑至少需要十年时间才能完全取代汽油税。

sentences.en: But it will probably come.
sentences.zh: 但它很可能会到来。

sentences.en: Infrastructure is all about choices.
sentences.zh: 基础设施关乎选择。

sentences.en: When a new bridge is proposed,
sentences.zh: 当提议修建一座新桥时，

sentences.en: there are countless discussions about whether the bridge should be purely functional,
sentences.zh: 会有无数关于这座桥是否应该纯粹出于功能性考虑的讨论，

sentences.en: and therefore presumably cheaper,
sentences.zh: 因此大概会更便宜，

sentences.en: or if it should be a signature piece of architecture that attracts international attention.
sentences.zh: 还是应该成为吸引国际关注的标志性建筑。

sentences.en: There are cases to be made on either side.
sentences.zh: 双方都有各自的理由。

sentences.en: I'm a signature man myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己是支持标志性建筑的。

sentences.en: But even mundane features like roads involve choices that reverberate for decades.
sentences.zh: 但即使是像道路这样平凡的设施，也涉及影响深远的选择。

sentences.en: Most roads today, that aren't interstate roads, are made of asphalt.
sentences.zh: 今天大多数非州际公路的道路都是用沥青铺成的。

sentences.en: One of asphalt's advantages, of course, is that it's seamless.
sentences.zh: 沥青的优点之一当然是无缝。

sentences.en: There is a real pleasure in driving on a new, smooth, black asphalt road.
sentences.zh: 在一条崭新、平坦、黑色的沥青路上行驶确实是一种享受。

sentences.en: Plus, asphalt can be laid down quickly, it's relatively cheap, and it's easy to patch and repair.
sentences.zh: 此外，沥青铺设速度快，相对便宜，而且容易修补。

sentences.en: The downside is, it's not especially durable.
sentences.zh: 缺点是它不是特别耐用。

sentences.en: You actually have to patch and repair it quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要经常修补它。

sentences.en: Alternatively, you can build a much more durable concrete road.
sentences.zh: 或者，你可以建造更耐用的混凝土道路。

sentences.en: But concrete doesn't offer that smooth, seamless ride that asphalt does.
sentences.zh: 但混凝土无法提供沥青那种平滑、无缝的驾驶体验。

sentences.en: Because, physics.
sentences.zh: 因为物理定律。

sentences.en: With concrete, we need what are so-called expansion joints,
sentences.zh: 对于混凝土，我们需要所谓的伸缩缝，

sentences.en: what appear to be cracks,
sentences.zh: 看起来像是裂缝，

sentences.en: but what are really deliberate lines cut into the concrete
sentences.zh: 但实际上是刻意切入混凝土的线条，

sentences.en: to allow it to crack in a controlled way.
sentences.zh: 以允许它以受控的方式开裂。

sentences.en: The cracks are there so that the road doesn't break into pieces
sentences.zh: 设置这些裂缝是为了让道路不会碎成块，

sentences.en: when the concrete contracts and expands due to big fluctuations in temperature.
sentences.zh: 当混凝土因温度剧烈波动而收缩和膨胀时。

sentences.en: But the tires of a vehicle going over them make a noise,
sentences.zh: 但车辆轮胎碾过它们时会发出噪音，

sentences.en: and the vehicle feels it.
sentences.zh: 车辆也能感觉到。

sentences.en: When you're driving on a concrete road, it sounds like,
sentences.zh: 当你行驶在混凝土路上时，听起来像是，

sentences.en: da-dun, da-dun, da-dun.
sentences.zh: 哒哒，哒哒，哒哒。

sentences.en: And the ride is not as smooth or as quiet as it can be on well-laid asphalt.
sentences.zh: 而且驾驶体验不如铺设良好的沥青路面平稳安静。

sentences.en: In addition, concrete roads are more expensive,
sentences.zh: 此外，混凝土道路更昂贵，

sentences.en: they're more expensive to repair, and they take longer.
sentences.zh: 维修成本更高，耗时也更长。

sentences.en: But they aren't as prone to potholes and can last a lot longer than asphalt roads.
sentences.zh: 但它们不容易出现坑洼，使用寿命比沥青路长得多。

sentences.en: So decisions have to be made.
sentences.zh: 所以必须做出决定。

sentences.en: Do we go with the cheaper, quicker, easier method and save money now?
sentences.zh: 我们是选择更便宜、更快、更简单的方法来节省眼前的开支吗？

sentences.en: Or go with the more expensive, slower, and less pleasing method
sentences.zh: 还是选择更昂贵、更慢、体验稍差的方法，

sentences.en: and hope to save money on repairs and replacement costs over time?
sentences.zh: 并希望随着时间的推移节省维修和更换成本？

sentences.en: Since so many of these decisions are made in a political context
sentences.zh: 由于这些决定大多是在政治背景下做出的，

sentences.en: by people who know that they are going to probably move on
sentences.zh: 决策者知道他们很可能在需要重新铺路之前

sentences.en: before the repaving has to be done,
sentences.zh: 就已经离职了，

sentences.en: we'll generally opt for the lesser expensive choice,
sentences.zh: 所以我们通常会选择成本较低的方案，

sentences.en: which means asphalt.
sentences.zh: 这意味着沥青。

sentences.en: Asphalt is simply cheaper than concrete.
sentences.zh: 沥青确实比混凝土便宜。

sentences.en: And therein is one of the main reasons
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们国家有这么多沥青路面的

sentences.en: that we have so much asphalt in this country.
sentences.zh: 主要原因之一。

sentences.en: But there is a more radical choice.
sentences.zh: 但还有一种更激进的选择。

sentences.en: In Montpelier, Vermont, there is a road called Bliss Road,
sentences.zh: 在佛蒙特州的蒙彼利埃，有一条路叫布利斯路（Bliss Road），

sentences.en: which was in a terrible state of disrepair for many years.
sentences.zh: 多年来一直处于极其破败的状态。

sentences.en: Until finally, in 2009, the city decided just to unpave the road,
sentences.zh: 直到2009年，市政府最终决定干脆把路面铲掉，

sentences.en: turn it into a dirt and gravel road.
sentences.zh: 把它变成一条土路和碎石路。

sentences.en: And since then, 27 states have also unpaved some of their roads
sentences.zh: 从那以后，又有27个州也铲掉了一些道路，

sentences.en: for the same reason.
sentences.zh: 原因也是一样。

sentences.en: I wondered if this was a clever solution or just a demoralizing defeat.
sentences.zh: 我当时在想，这究竟是个聪明的解决方案，还是一次令人沮丧的失败。

sentences.en: I've heard about that, and it does seem like a pretty clever solution.
sentences.zh: 我听说过这件事，这看起来确实是个相当聪明的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's probably not a very popular solution among the paving contractors, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，这对铺路承包商来说可能并不是一个受欢迎的方案。

sentences.en: It would depend on the nature of this road.
sentences.zh: 这得取决于这条路的性质。

sentences.en: If this is a road that doesn't have especially heavy traffic,
sentences.zh: 如果这条路的车流量不是特别大，

sentences.en: not a lot of heavy truck traffic,
sentences.zh: 没有太多重型卡车通行，

sentences.en: it might work from an engineering point of view.
sentences.zh: 从工程角度来看，这或许行得通。

sentences.en: When the eastern span of the Bay Bridge was about to open in 2013,
sentences.zh: 2013年海湾大桥东段即将通车时，

sentences.en: they set aside a day for pedestrians to walk the bridge,
sentences.zh: 他们专门留出一天时间让行人步行通过大桥，

sentences.en: much like people did in 1883 when the Brooklyn Bridge was opened.
sentences.zh: 就像1883年布鲁克林大桥开通时人们所做的那样。

sentences.en: I was all set to bring my kids,
sentences.zh: 我当时已经准备好带孩子们去了，

sentences.en: celebrate this new massive piece of infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 去庆祝这一宏大的新基础设施落成。

sentences.en: But because of last-minute repairs, the event was canceled,
sentences.zh: 但由于最后一刻的维修工作，活动被取消了，

sentences.en: and the bridge opened to traffic with much less public involvement in the fanfare.
sentences.zh: 大桥在公众参与度极低的情况下通车了，也没什么庆祝活动。

sentences.en: And I really didn't get a sense that people were all that upset about it.
sentences.zh: 我真的没感觉到人们对此有多么不满。

sentences.en: We collectively just don't have the feeling that infrastructure warrants celebration
sentences.zh: 我们集体不再觉得基础设施值得庆祝，

sentences.en: or a sense of pride like we once did.
sentences.zh: 也不再像过去那样感到自豪了。

sentences.en: I asked Dr. Petrosky why he thought that is.
sentences.zh: 我问了佩特罗斯基（Petrosky）博士，他认为这是为什么。

sentences.en: Oh, I think we, the electorate, has gotten mentally lazy about the infrastructure like we have about a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 哦，我认为我们这些选民在基础设施问题上变得思想懒惰了，就像我们在很多事情上一样。

sentences.en: We tend to focus on what's of immediate concern to us.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于关注与我们切身相关的事情。

sentences.en: We might worry more about our driveway than the highway that is nearby.
sentences.zh: 我们可能更关心自家车道，而不是附近的公路。

sentences.en: I do think that celebratory events are important and that do help generate that pride and almost responsibility
sentences.zh: 我确实认为庆祝活动很重要，它们有助于激发那种自豪感，甚至是一种责任感，

sentences.en: because everybody's a part of all this.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都是这一切的一部分。

sentences.en: The different things that we vote for and pay for in our taxes and fees,
sentences.zh: 我们通过税收和费用投票支持并支付的各种项目，

sentences.en: we're really part owner of all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们其实都是这些东西的共同所有者。

sentences.en: And we should worry about it as much as we do our neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我们应该像关心社区一样关心它们。

sentences.en: What do you think about the idea of reclaiming the term public works,
sentences.zh: 你觉得重新启用“公共工程”（public works）这个词怎么样？

sentences.en: you know, to reflect the fact that it is owned by all of us and that it is public?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为了反映它属于我们所有人，而且是公共财产这一事实？

sentences.en: That's a good idea.
sentences.zh: 这是个好主意。

sentences.en: I haven't given it a great deal of thought, but that would make it more explicit.
sentences.zh: 我还没深入思考过，但这会让它表达得更明确。

sentences.en: It's for the public and by the public in a way.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它是为了公众，也由公众所有。

sentences.en: The infrastructure is such a, what is it, a Latinate word that, you know, makes it more abstract and removed.
sentences.zh: “基础设施”（infrastructure）这个词，怎么说呢，是个拉丁语系的词汇，让人觉得更抽象、更疏远。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's an interesting idea.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这是个有趣的想法。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Well, I just thought of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我刚想到的。

sentences.en: Oh, good.
sentences.zh: 哦，不错。

sentences.en: Well, excellent.
sentences.zh: 嗯，太棒了。

sentences.en: I have a proposal to send out into the world.
sentences.zh: 我有一个提议要向全世界发布。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is Sam Greenspan, Delaney Hall, Kurt Kolstad, Taryn Mazza, Katie Mingle, Avery Truffleman, Sharif Youssef, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》的成员包括山姆·格林斯潘（Sam Greenspan）、德莱尼·霍尔（Delaney Hall）、库尔特·科尔斯塔德（Kurt Kolstad）、塔琳·马扎（Taryn Mazza）、凯蒂·明格尔（Katie Mingle）、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼（Avery Truffleman）、谢里夫·优素福（Sharif Youssef），以及我，罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Oliver Assis for answering some questions about pavement I had on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢奥利弗·阿西斯（Oliver Assis）在推特上回答了我关于路面的一些问题。

sentences.en: We use music this week from the trifecta of 99PI All-Stars.
sentences.zh: 本周我们使用了来自《99PI》全明星三人组的音乐。

sentences.en: That's Okeakumi, Lollatone, and Melodium.
sentences.zh: 他们是Okeakumi、Lollatone和Melodium。

sentences.en: Buy their music and make your life better.
sentences.zh: 去买他们的音乐，让你的生活更美好。

sentences.en: We'll have links on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们的网站上会有链接。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW电台的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的“广播街”（Radio Row）制作。

sentences.en: You can find this show and talk about this show on Facebook and follow us all on Twitter
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并讨论这个节目，也可以在推特上关注我们，

sentences.en: and Instagram.
sentences.zh: 还有Instagram。

sentences.en: Our Tumblr curates cool design stories from around the web, but the easiest way to listen
sentences.zh: 我们的Tumblr会精选来自网络各处的酷炫设计故事，但最简单的收听方式

sentences.en: to all the past episodes and read more cool stories about design is to go to our website.
sentences.zh: 是访问我们的网站，收听所有往期节目并阅读更多关于设计的精彩故事。

sentences.en: It's 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 网址是99PI.org。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
